prose.summary: The aluminium window frames qualify for the preferential customs duty rate under the India-UAE CEPA. Claiming the CEPA rate for this shipment results in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED. Please refer to the claim checklist below to complete the necessary steps for claiming this preference.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, which covers doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium), with high confidence. You should confirm this HS code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving on this shipment is 10000.00 AED. The CEPA rate applies only to Basic Customs Duty, so other import charges such as IGST are still paid even when the CEPA rate is 0%.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH), where each non-originating input must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the product, plus value addition (VA) of at least 45% on an FOB basis. The product meets this rule because the final manufacture check passed, confirming the last manufacturing step took place in the UAE, and the minimal operations check passed, meaning the UAE work goes beyond simple operations. Additionally, all 3 non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, and the value addition is 49.0%, which exceeds the 45% threshold.

notes.text: The CEPA rate reduces only the Basic Customs Duty and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess for Table II lines. Other charges such as IGST, GST compensation cess, and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply, although a lower Basic Customs Duty reduces the IGST base. Any anti-dumping, countervailing, or safeguard duties also remain applicable.

The acceptance of electronic certificates and their upload to India's e-Sanchit system is based on CBIC Instruction 28/2022. Mansha has only read this instruction through secondary reports and not from the official text.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD), and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply, as do any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties. Because the IGST base includes BCD, a lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
